rfp_analysis.detected_priority_note: The RFP rules out a database migration and asks for rollout with minimal disruption. Proposals that change NordFrame’s infrastructure should lose points.

requirements.text: A web-based dashboard showing real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses.
Alerts to warehouse managers when items fall below a configurable threshold.
Integration with the existing PostgreSQL inventory database, with no migration to a new database.
requirements.source_quote: no migration to a new database

requirements.text: Warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all sites.
A data migration / onboarding plan for all 6 sites with minimal disruption.
Support and maintenance terms after go-live, including response times and SLAs.
Clear documentation of assumptions, limitations or risks, since inventory decisions will rely on the system.
€80,000–€120,000 total, including the first year of support.
requirements.source_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

requirements.text: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months; all 6 sites within 6 months.
requirements.source_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The RFP lists seven numbered requirements and puts each one in bold. A buyer who writes a checklist reads the answer as a checklist.

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Dependencies and risks are flagged, not hidden.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Requirement 7 explains why it is asked for, which is rare. The client is telling you that hidden risk is the thing they fear.

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Pricing Clarity
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Price stated, broken down, easy to follow.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The budget is published as a range and states that it includes the first year of support, so a vague price is easy to spot.

source_refs.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Timeline Clarity
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Two hard dates are given: a pilot at one site within 3 months and all 6 sites within 6 months.

source_refs.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Says how inventory figures are checked against reality before anyone relies on them.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The RFP does not list this as a requirement, but it gives the reason behind Requirement 7: stock decisions will be made from this dashboard. A proposal that never says how the numbers are verified leaves that risk with the client.

scoring.verdict: It contradicts the no-migration constraint, adds AI modules nobody asked for, and promises 8-week delivery with no pilot, at a price that can’t cover that scope.

criteria.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
criteria.comment: Contradicts requirement 3, leaves 4, 5 and 7 unaddressed, and covers 2 and 6 only partly.

criteria.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
criteria.comment: A database migration and an 8-week schedule are the riskiest items here, and neither comes with a single assumption or risk.

criteria.name: Pricing Clarity
criteria.comment: €98,000 is inside the budget but claims to cover a migration, three AI modules and a year of support, with no breakdown.
citations: covering the full suite described above

criteria.name: Timeline Clarity
criteria.comment: Concrete but not credible: 8 weeks for a platform migration plus all AI modules, and no pilot phase.
citations: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

criteria.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
criteria.comment: Proposes moving the data to another platform with no validation step anywhere, while adding forecasting on top of figures nobody has checked.
citations: migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database

criteria.name: Problem Understanding
criteria.comment: Reframes a dashboard brief as an “AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Suite”. The client asked for continuity and minimal disruption.
citations: NordFrame deserves more than a simple dashboard
no migration to a new database

criteria.name: Scope & Deliverables Clarity
criteria.comment: Scope grows to forecasting, automated reordering and supplier scoring, none of it requested, while role-based access and onboarding are left out.

criteria.name: Tone & Persuasiveness
criteria.comment: Hype-driven, and it implies the client’s own brief is too small.
citations: full power of modern machine learning

criteria.name: Legacy System & Spreadsheets
criteria.comment: Silent on the legacy system and the spreadsheets, although it proposes replacing the database they feed.

findings.reason: Promises “real-time alerts” in general, not low-stock alerts with configurable thresholds sent to warehouse managers.
findings.citation: Real-time alerts across all locations simultaneously
findings.suggested_patch: Replace with: “Low-stock alerts: warehouse managers are notified when an item falls below a threshold they configure per item.”

findings.reason: Recommends “migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database” to a proprietary platform. The RFP says “no migration to a new database”.
findings.citation: migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database
findings.suggested_patch: Remove the platform migration and state: “The dashboard connects to your existing PostgreSQL inventory database; no data is migrated.” If a new platform is worth raising, move it to an optional, separately priced “Later phases” note.

findings.reason: No user roles or site-level access are described.
findings.suggested_patch: Add: “Role-based access: warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all 6 sites.”

findings.reason: The only migration described is of the data platform. There is no plan for rolling out to the 6 sites with minimal disruption.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a rollout plan: pilot at one warehouse, a parallel run, then the remaining sites in batches, with dates.

findings.reason: “One year of support” is included, with no response times or SLAs.
findings.suggested_patch: Add response times per severity and support hours for the included year.

findings.reason: No risks are disclosed, despite a proposed database migration and an 8-week schedule.
findings.suggested_patch: Add “Risks & assumptions” covering data migration risk, access to supplier systems for reordering, and how much sales history the forecasting model needs.

findings.reason: €98,000 is inside the budget but is said to cover a platform migration, three AI modules and a year of support, with no breakdown.
findings.citation: covering the full suite described above
findings.suggested_patch: Price the requested scope on its own with a line-item breakdown; list forecasting, reordering and supplier scoring as optional add-ons with separate prices.

findings.reason: 8 weeks for the full suite including a migration, and no pilot. The client asked for a pilot at one site within 3 months, then rollout within 6.
findings.suggested_patch: Follow the client’s phasing: pilot at one warehouse by Month 3, all 6 sites by Month 6, with milestones. Drop “well ahead of typical industry timelines” unless a comparable project backs it.
